summary: Eduard Schwyzer was a linguist and Indologist who succeeded Adolf Kaegi in 1914. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (circa 1912–1927), the University of Bonn (circa 1927–1932), and the University of Berlin (circa 1932–1943).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied for a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under MA supervisors Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Edvard Westermarck worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (circa 1881–1889) and held posts at the London School of Economics (circa 1904–1930) and Åbo Akademi University (circa 1918–1932).

Edward Albert Gait was a historian and Indologist who studied at University College London (circa 1880–1882). In 1914 he founded the Bihar and Orissa Research Society, serving as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. Educated at Charterhouse School, Merton College, and the University of Oxford, he held posts at the East India Company College (1845) and Foreign Office (circa 1860–1863).

Edward Byles Cowell, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served as principal of Sanskrit College and University, taught at Presidency College, and was a professor at Cambridge from 1867 to 1903.

Edward C. Dimock Jr. was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale and Harvard (Ph.D. 1959). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Chicago (1966–1993) and president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972–1986).

Edward Capps studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. During his academic career, he held positions at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale University (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).

Edward Clive Bayley was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the East India Company College (Haileybury and Imperial Service College) circa 1840–1842 and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Cologne. He held posts at the University of London, University of Wisconsin-Madison, UC Berkeley, and Lancaster University, and was Vice-President of The Buddhist Society.

Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University (circa 1871–1875) and the University of Tübingen (circa 1877–1879), and served as Jay Professor at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

Edward Denison Ross was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies who studied at UCL and Strasbourg. He held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the National Archives of India, and served as Director of SOAS (1916–1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale and in Europe under Eugène Burnouf and Franz Bopp. He served as Professor at Yale (1841–1854) and was President of the American Oriental Society (1873–1880).

Edward Espe Brown is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shunryu Suzuki, Reb Anderson, and Sojun Mel Weitsman. He served as manager, cook, and Zen teacher at the San Francisco Zen Center, Tassajara, and Green Gulch Farm.

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Granville Browne was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Cambridge under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell. He was a Fellow of Pembroke College, Cambridge Lecturer in Persian (1888), and Adams Professor of Arabic (1902).

Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Harvard. He was a professor at UC Berkeley from circa 1947 to 1984 and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

Edward Hamilton Johnston was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at New College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1908–1921) and was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1937–1942).

Edward John Garrett is a linguist and Tibetologist. He completed his Ph.D. at UCLA under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, and held research assistant positions at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Joseph Thomas was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a master's at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet and studied at Cambridge, where he later worked at the library and served as departmental Dean (1909–1939).
